newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican soybean demand seen increasing in future.
newsitem.headline: Mexican soybean demand seen increasing in future.

text.p: Mexican soybean demand, with its implied import need, is seen increasing in the future, a survey carried out by the local office of the American Soybean Association (ASA) said Wednesday.

Among oil crushers surveyed by the ASA, 68 percent said they expected future soybean use at "increased volumes". Only six percent said they saw "decreased volumes" and 26 percent eyed "same volumes as before".
Among food processors, 80 percent said they envisaged the use of soybean products at "same volumes" and 20 percent at increased volumes. None saw volumes decreasing.
A majority 55 percent of the companies surveyed said they use other oilseeds in conjunction with soybeans. The remaining 45 percent processed or used soybean products only.

Of the companies reporting using other oilseed products in addition to soybeans, 27 percent said they chose sunflower, 27 percent cottonseed, 23 percent safflower, 18 percent palm oil, 4.5 percent canola and 4.5 percent corn.
--Chris Aspin, Mexico City newsroom (525) 7289530. E-mail at chris.aspin@reuters.com
